proposal.reactor_type: Stainless-steel coil reactor with external heating jacket (no microwave); thermal activation replaces microwave dielectric heating
proposal.residence_time_basis: Reactor volume divided by total volumetric flow rate of combined reagent streams at operating temperature
proposal.light_setup: Not applicable — thermal Suzuki-Miyaura coupling; no photochemical activation required

streams.stream_label: Stream A — Aryl Bromide + Pd Catalyst
streams.contents: Aromatic bromide (0.16 M) + Pd(PPh3)4 (0.03 M, 3 mol % relative to ArBr) dissolved in anhydrous DMF
streams.solvent: DMF (anhydrous, degassed by sparging with N2 for 15 min)

streams.contents: Phenylboronic acid derivative (0.24 M, 1.5 equiv) + K2CO3 (0.48 M, 3.0 equiv) dissolved in DMF/H2O 9:1 v/v
streams.phase: liquid (homogeneous; K2CO3 partially soluble — use finely ground powder and sonicate; alternatively substitute Cs2CO3 for full solubility)

proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer (PEEK, 0.5 mm bore) followed by 10 cm pre-heat zone before reactor coil
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Aryl bromide and Pd catalyst are kept separate from the base until the T-mixer to prevent premature protodeboronation of the boronic acid under basic conditions and to avoid catalyst precipitation. The base and boronic acid are co-dissolved in Stream B because K2CO3 activates the boronate in situ; this is the standard Suzuki activation pathway. Streams A and B are combined at the T-mixer immediately before the heated reactor coil.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas both solvent reservoirs by N2 sparging (≥15 min) to remove dissolved O2 that would oxidize Pd(0) to inactive Pd(II) species
Prepare Stream A fresh and protect from light and air; use sealed syringes under N2 blanket
Sonicate Stream B to dissolve K2CO3 fully or switch to Cs2CO3 (more soluble in DMF/H2O) to prevent pump blockage
Prime both pumps and purge dead volume with solvent before introducing reagents
Set BPR to 6.9 bar (100 psi) to suppress DMF vapor (bp 153 °C) and maintain single liquid phase at 80 °C
post_reactor_steps: Effluent passes through BPR (6.9 bar) to maintain back-pressure throughout reactor
Collect effluent in a sealed vial under N2 to prevent oxidation of any residual Pd(0)
Quench with saturated NH4Cl(aq) to neutralize base and precipitate inorganic salts
Extract with EtOAc (3×); wash organic layer with brine
Filter through short pad of Celite/silica to remove Pd black and inorganic residues
Concentrate under reduced pressure; purify by column chromatography or recrystallization if needed
Pd leaching check: ICP-MS on product solution if pharmaceutical application
chemistry_notes: Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling: ArBr + ArB(OH)2 → Ar-Ar + B(OH)3 + KBr, catalyzed by Pd(0)/Pd(II) cycle
Microwave at 50 °C for 10 min in batch is equivalent to ~80 °C for 10 min in flow due to superior heat transfer in narrow-bore tubing (no microwave-specific non-thermal effect is assumed)
Temperature increase from 50 °C to 80 °C compensates for loss of microwave superheating and ensures comparable or faster kinetics in flow
DMF chosen to match batch solvent; 10% water added to Stream B to dissolve inorganic base and facilitate transmetalation
Pd(PPh3)4 used as air-sensitive but highly active catalyst; Pd(dppf)Cl2 or Pd(OAc)2/SPhos are viable alternatives with better air stability
No gas stream required; reaction is fully liquid-phase
Concentration set at 0.16 M (ArBr) to match batch scale (1.6 mmol in ~10 mL total volume equivalent) while keeping flow manageable
Assumption: batch yield of 91% is achievable in flow at 80 °C / 10 min; optimization of temperature (60–100 °C) and residence time (5–20 min) recommended in first flow experiments

stage_2_pre_heat_zone.device: 10 cm SS coil in heating jacket

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Directly matched to batch reaction time of 10 min; flow heat transfer is superior so this is conservative — shorter times (5–7 min) may suffice at 80 °C
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Total flow = 0.10 + 0.10 = 0.20 mL/min; chosen to give exactly 10 min residence in 2.0 mL reactor (V = Q × t → 2.0 = 0.20 × 10)
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Elevated from batch 50 °C to 80 °C to compensate for absence of microwave dielectric heating; DMF bp is 153 °C so no boiling risk at 80 °C; BPR provides additional safety margin
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.16 M ArBr in Stream A; after mixing 1:1 with Stream B, effective concentration in reactor is 0.08 M ArBr — dilute enough to prevent precipitation but concentrated enough for practical throughput
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 6.9 bar (100 psi) chosen to keep DMF well below boiling point at 80 °C and to maintain single-phase flow; DMF vapor pressure at 80 °C is ~0.05 bar so 6.9 bar provides >100× safety margin
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Coil reactor preferred over chip for ease of Pd-catalyst handling and resistance to fouling; stainless steel tolerates DMF and base
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: 316L SS is compatible with DMF, K2CO3, and Pd catalysts; PEEK would also work but SS gives better thermal conductivity
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID gives good mixing via Taylor flow and manageable back-pressure; narrower bore risks blockage from K2CO3 particles
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 2.0 mL = 0.20 mL/min × 10 min; coil length = V / (π × (ID/2)²) = 2000 mm³ / (π × 0.25 mm²) ≈ 2546 mm ≈ 2.55 m of 1.0 mm ID tubing
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_safety: BPR prevents flash evaporation of DMF and maintains defined residence time by preventing gas bubble formation
reasoning_per_field.concentration_reasoning: Batch: 1.6 mmol in ~10 mL DMF = 0.16 M; replicated in Stream A; boronic acid at 1.5 equiv = 0.24 M in Stream B
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: No photochemical step; thermal Pd catalysis only
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: T-mixer ensures rapid initial mixing; pre-heat zone equilibrates temperature before main reactor coil

literature_analogies: Glasnov, T.N.; Kappe, C.O. 'Microwave-Assisted Synthesis under Continuous-Flow Conditions' Macromol. Rapid Commun. 2007, 28, 395–410 — demonstrates translation of microwave batch Suzuki couplings to continuous flow with comparable yields
Ceylan, S. et al. 'Inductive Heating for Organic Synthesis' Chem. Eur. J. 2011, 17, 1884 — Suzuki coupling in flow at 80–100 °C, 10 min residence, DMF/H2O, Pd catalyst, >85% yield

Hartman, R.L. et al. 'Deciding Whether To Go with the Flow' Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2011, 50, 7502 — general framework for batch-to-flow translation including temperature compensation for microwave reactions
Noël, T.; Buchwald, S.L. 'Cross-coupling in flow' Chem. Soc. Rev. 2011, 40, 5010 — Pd-catalyzed cross-couplings in microreactors, residence times 5–15 min, temperatures 60–100 °C
safety_flags: DMF is a reproductive toxin (Category 1B); use in closed flow system with solvent trap on exhaust; avoid skin contact; work in fume hood
Pd(PPh3)4 is air- and moisture-sensitive; handle under inert atmosphere; PPh3 is a mild irritant
K2CO3 slurry risk: fine particles can block pump check valves and tubing; use filtered solutions or switch to Cs2CO3
Pressure: system operates at 6.9 bar; use pressure-rated fittings and tubing rated to ≥20 bar; install pressure relief valve upstream of BPR rated at 15 bar
Temperature: 80 °C heating jacket; use insulated housing; label hot surfaces
Pd black fouling: reactor coil may accumulate Pd nanoparticles over extended runs; flush with dilute HCl/DMF periodically
Waste: Pd-containing waste must be collected separately for precious metal recovery; DMF waste requires incineration
Leak detection: install solvent sensor under reactor; DMF is flammable (flash point 58 °C) — keep away from ignition sources

Scale-up note: at 0.20 mL/min, throughput is ~1.6 mmol per 10 min (matching batch); for higher throughput, increase concentration or use parallel reactors rather than increasing flow rate beyond pump limits
